entry_state: The debt argument ends with issuance costs, feasible supply, policy-consistent pricing and dated missed-payment memory. Equal closing statements can conceal different repayment histories, and a payment does not itself establish contractual cure or rescission. The equity chapter now distinguishes book equity, market value, legal share capital and the share count created by a cash issue.
exit_state: Equity funding now has explicit price, fee, quantity, class-right and holder consequences. Percentage dilution differs from value transfer; conversion, repurchase, dividends and control require their own dated rules. The next chapter maps economic events into postings and reports, beginning with an accrual sale whose later collection is not new revenue.

observations.finding: The issue-price, fee/cap, preference-waterfall, conversion and repurchase examples preserve separate cash and share consequences. The preference threshold is 120 and the gross issuance/repurchase example nets 80 cash and ten shares, not a genuine issue at eight.
observations.disposition: retain; rights and terms are expressly supplied assumptions

observations.finding: Section 6.11 says using 120 closing shares instead of the 110 weighted average understates basic EPS without stating positive earnings. For a negative numerator it makes loss per share less negative, so the direction reverses.
observations.disposition: confirmed sign-qualification omission; specify positive earnings and explain the loss case in the current bounded successor

observations.finding: The financing comparison yields seven shares and zero closing cash; a six-share cap leaves five unpaid. Share-register and conformance duties are separated from fair pricing, investor demand, legal approval and actual management behavior.
observations.disposition: retain; no statistical or legal validity is inferred from conservation checks

observations.finding: The event chapter starts with separate occurrence, recognition, settlement and reporting times. A sale of 30 with cost 18 changes receivables and profit before collection, so later receipt cannot be recognized as a second sale.
observations.disposition: retain; continue the full event/report argument
